summary: FDIR/OIT assessment of an ordered sequence of retained window innovations

domain_rules.rule: One residual sequence must share an identical scope (channel, frame, units, clock, calibration, model, reference prior); targets strictly increase; no GSIE result, physical window or sample set counts twice; a repeated observation id cannot change content

The analytic oracle re-derives NIS, whitened residual, ambiguous isolability, two-sided CUSUM with reset, and trivial 1x1 observability, then compares at rel_tol 2e-12 / abs_tol 1e-14 with exact integers
Stateful CUSUM across windows, advanced only when OIT reports 'observable' (observability hold does not advance the state); interpretation flags are fixed to limited authority
Overlap annotations record interval overlap and shared observation/artifact ids, with residual_cross_covariance declared unknown

The monitor reads calibrated-window's internal step layout: GSIE at child['steps'][3] (133), and mapped event times from the CIW-wrapped TBRT data at child['steps'][0]['result']['data']['samples'] (180). It also builds the OIT declaration from the upstream GSIE dynamics and observation matrices (192-194).
domain_rules.evidence: added by adversarial verification; citations in the rule

domain_rules.rule: Upstreams are validated in depth, again and again. _unwrap re-runs acquired_window._validate, calibrated_window._validate and _check_child_receipt for every selected window (106-119). That happens at create (478), at every reopen (_validate calls validate_upstreams at 455), and again at link time against the catalog (workbench.py:377-378).
domain_rules.evidence: added by adversarial verification; citations in the rule

domain_rules.rule: In the bootstrap, CUSUM state advances only when OIT returns 'observable'; the pre and post state is recorded, and the interpretation flags are fixed (bootstrap roughly 230-250). This is a fold over the windows that carries state from one to the next.
domain_rules.evidence: added by adversarial verification; citations in the rule
